title: Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance?

paper.authors: He, Rungta, Koleczek, Sekhon, Wang, Hasan (Microsoft / MIT)
paper.repo_note: No code release; the only GitHub link in the PDF (github.com/openai/evals) is a third-party tool cited for the NER Finance data.

dependence.note: The finding is the sensitivity of four Azure OpenAI GPT snapshots to prompt format; every number is model output under a fixed benchmark.

claim.statement: Prompt format (plain text / Markdown / YAML / JSON) significantly changes task performance for all four GPT models (one-sided matched-pair t-tests p < 0.05 in every dataset x model cell except GPT-4-1106-preview on HumanEval, p = 0.055; Table 1), and GPT-4-1106-preview ('GPT-4-turbo') is less sensitive than GPT-3.5: e.g. MMLU 81.2 (Markdown) vs 73.9 (JSON) for GPT-4-1106-preview, while GPT-35-turbo-0613 swings 59.7 (JSON) vs 50.0 (Markdown) on MMLU and 200-300% on FIND / HumanEval (Sec. 3.2, Tables 1, 3, 4).
claim.metric: Task score per format (MMLU accuracy over 57 subjects; HumanEval pass@1 with unit tests; NER Finance entity score; CODEXGLUE Java<->C# translation score; HumanEval-X; FIND score), best-vs-worst format gap and matched-pair t-test p-value; consistency and IoU metrics in Secs. 4-5
claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 (sensitivity), Tables 3-8 (per-format scores with SD), Sec. 2.3 (models)

protocol.model: Azure OpenAI deployments gpt-35-turbo-0613, gpt-35-turbo-16k-0613, gpt-4-32k-0613, gpt-4-1106-preview (Sec. 2.3). 'GPT-4-turbo' in the text = gpt-4-1106-preview. gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 NOT used (only the 0125 laziness fix is mentioned in passing, Appendix D).
protocol.model_status: dead (gpt-4-1106-preview 2026-03-26; gpt-4-32k 2025-06-06; gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 / 16k 2024-09-13). Live arm not an experimental arm.
protocol.endpoint: Azure OpenAI chat completions (deployment names above); API version not reported
protocol.prompt_source: appendix Table 2 (four format templates with persona / instructions / examples / output-format / user-ask placeholders) and Appendix C examples - paper only, no files

params.n_runs: not reported (SDs in Tables 3-8 appear to be across subjects/items, not seeds)

protocol.n_items: MMLU 14,079 test questions; HumanEval 164; NER Finance 500 sampled; FIND 500 functions; CODEXGLUE 1,000 pairs per direction; HumanEval-X 164; each x 4 formats
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: accuracy / pass@1 via unit tests / string-match entity scoring / translation similarity; matched-pair t-test across items between best and worst format.
protocol.environment_check: not applicable - no artifacts; a successor run would need our own reimplementation of the four templates from Table 2 and Appendix C

artifacts.data_license: underlying benchmarks public (MMLU MIT, HumanEval MIT, CodeXGLUE C-UDA/MIT, HumanEval-X Apache-2.0, FIND MIT, NER Finance from openai/evals MIT); the formatted prompt files, sampled subsets and outputs are not released
artifacts.notes: Template skeletons are printed in Table 2 and Appendix C, so a faithful-in-spirit reimplementation is feasible; exact wording of ICL examples and output-format instructions per task is only partially shown.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: all four Azure snapshots are dead ('GPT-4-turbo' = gpt-4-1106-preview)
no code, prompt files, sampled subsets (NER 500, FIND 500) or outputs released
decoding parameters and number of runs unreported
Azure deployment behaviour (content filters, API version) not reproducible on the public OpenAI endpoint

full_hypothetical.note: all 6 datasets x 4 formats x 3 seeds (16,607 items x 4 x 3); ~600 in / ~200 out tokens (CoT-style outputs); HYPOTHETICAL, card is blocked

representative_subset.note: HumanEval (164) + 1,000-item stratified MMLU subset, x 4 formats x 3 seeds = 4,656 calls/seed; preserves the GPT-4 MMLU Markdown-vs-JSON gap and the HumanEval non-significance cell

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1 on the GPT-4 MMLU cell: survival = best-vs-worst format gap same sign (Markdown/plain > JSON) with matched-pair p < 0.05 and gap of the same order (~7 points); partial = significant but gap collapses to < 2 points or reorders formats; dead = no significant format effect. Secondary: HumanEval cell remains non-significant (p > 0.05).
judgment.notes: Only judgeable on successor models; no live baseline.

status_reason: live model not an experimental arm (the paper's 'GPT-4-turbo' is gpt-4-1106-preview; all snapshots dead); no artifacts

domain_notes: A prompt-sensitivity study on Azure-hosted GPT snapshots, all now retired; the models are subjects. The paper reports enough template structure to rebuild the four formats but not the exact per-task ICL examples, so any re-execution is a conceptual replication. The scaffold's 'gpt-4-turbo' hit is the paper's shorthand for gpt-4-1106-preview (alias false positive).
